# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q1.3

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Accounting P1, November 2025, question Q1.3.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2025. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (36 marks)

Prepare the Statement of Financial Position on 28 February 2025. NOTE: Show ALL workings in brackets. Certain figures are provided in the ANSWER BOOK. Missing amounts in shaded areas must NOT be filled in. (The ANSWER BOOK pre-prints the format with Current assets 5 798 000, Trade and other receivables opening with 735 000, and Trade and other payables opening with 878 500; the lines for Fixed assets at carrying value, Cash and cash equivalents, Total assets, and the fixed-asset figure are among the shaded/blank areas.)

(The information was taken from the accounting records of Violet Limited. The financial year ended on 28 February 2025.)

Information, summarised:

- A. Balances on 28 February 2025 (with 29 February 2024 comparatives where given): Fixed deposit: Time Bank unknown; Trading stock 4 598 000; Debtors' control 735 000; Provision for bad debts unknown; Ordinary shareholders' equity unknown (16 200 000 in 2024); Ordinary share capital 17 875 000 (11 395 000 in 2024); Retained income unknown (4 805 000 in 2024); Mortgage loan: Delta Bank 3 200 000; Creditors' control 878 500; Bank (unfavourable) unknown.
- B. Trading stock: the closing stock of one brand of men's informal shirts, shown at R285 500 on the first-in-first-out method, must be corrected to the weighted-average method (the corrected value, from Q1.1, is R272 240).
- C. Fixed deposit: Time Bank: a fixed deposit of R320 000 matured on 31 July 2025; the remaining 60% of the fixed deposit will mature on 31 December 2028.
- D. A debtor who had overpaid his account by R5 000 in the Debtors' Ledger requested that the overpayment be transferred to his account in the Creditors' Ledger; this transfer has not yet been recorded. The provision for bad debts must be adjusted to 4% of the outstanding debtors.
- E. Extract from the Statement of Comprehensive Income for the year (already adjusted): Commission income 169 400; Rent income 430 500; Directors' fees 1 998 750. The adjustments taken into account were: commission income of R6 400 for February 2025 still outstanding; rent for March and April 2025 received and recorded, with the rent increased by 10% on 1 December 2024; two directors earned the same monthly fee all year and were paid in full, while a third director, Jack Jele, employed on 1 June 2024 at a monthly fee 25% lower than the others, was paid up to 31 March 2025.
- F. Mortgage loan: Delta Bank: fixed monthly repayments of R45 000, including capitalised interest, were made and correctly recorded for the year; the monthly repayments stay the same until the loan is repaid in approximately four years; interest for the next financial year is expected to be R290 000.
- G. Shares and dividends (already recorded): authorised share capital 9 000 000 shares; 750 000 new shares issued on 31 March 2024; an interim dividend paid on 1 September 2024; 150 000 shares repurchased on 31 January 2025 with EFT payments totalling R1 710 000; a final dividend of 90 cents per share declared on the 2 750 000 shares in issue on 28 February 2025.
- H. The SARS assessment for the year indicated a tax refund of R70 000; the net profit after tax was accurately calculated to be R4 721 700.
- I. Financial indicators calculated on 28 February 2025 after all of the above: current ratio 1,3 : 1; % return on average shareholders' equity 24%.

## Method

statement of financial position with adjustments

## Memo working

Non-current assets — Fixed deposit: Time Bank: the R320 000 that matured on 31 July 2025 is a current asset, and it represents 40% of the deposit, so the non-current portion is (320 000 x 60/40) OR 800 000 - 320 000 = 480 000 (2 marks).

Current assets (pre-printed total 5 798 000) — Inventories: 4 598 000 (one mark) - 13 260 (one mark) [that is, - 285 500 + 272 240, the corrected stock from Q1.1, one mark + one method mark; if the Q1.1 answer is greater than the closing stock, the sign should be positive] = 4 584 740 (one part correct).

Trade and other receivables: 735 000 + 5 000 (transfer of the overpaid debtor's credit balance to the Creditors' Ledger) - 29 600 (provision for bad debts, 4% x 740 000) + 6 400 (commission income accrued) + 48 750 (directors' fees prepaid: 30,75 monthly fees make up the 1 998 750 expense, so a monthly fee is 65 000; Jack Jele's fee is 75% x 65 000 = 48 750, and he was paid for March 2025 in advance) + 70 000 (SARS income tax refund) = 835 550 (one part correct). [Assets section: 12 marks.]

Shareholders' equity: the average equity is 4 721 700 x 100/24 = 19 673 750, so closing equity is [(4 721 700 x 100/24) x 2] = 39 347 500 (three marks) - 16 200 000 = 23 147 500 (one part correct). Ordinary share capital 17 875 000 (see Q1.2). Retained income 5 272 500 = shareholders' equity minus ordinary share capital; can be negative. [Equity block: 7 marks.]

Non-current liabilities — Mortgage loan: Delta Bank: 3 200 000 + 290 000 - 540 000 [the year's repayments of 45 000 x 12; the capital portion repayable next year is 540 000 - 290 000 = 250 000, three marks] = 2 950 000 (one part correct). [5 marks.]

Current liabilities: from the current ratio of 1,3 : 1, total current liabilities = 5 798 000 / 1,3 = 4 460 000. Trade and other payables: 878 500 + 5 000 (transfer) + 77 000 (rent income received in advance: 12,3 months' rent make up the 430 500 income, so the rent was 35 000 per month before the 10% increase and 38 500 after; March and April 2025 at 38 500 each = 77 000) = 960 500 (one part correct). Current portion of loan: (540 000 - 290 000) = 250 000 (see non-current liabilities). Shareholders for dividends: (2 750 000 x 90/100) = 2 475 000. Bank overdraft 774 500 (balancing figure: 4 460 000 - 960 500 - 250 000 - 2 475 000; can be negative). [Current liabilities block: 10 marks.]

(Memo: inspect — current portion of loan and shareholders for dividends may be included in Trade and other payables. -1 foreign items, max -2; -1 presentation, max -1; misplaced items award marks for workings only.)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

Fixed deposit: Time Bank 480 000; Current assets 5 798 000; Inventories 4 584 740; Trade and other receivables 835 550; Shareholders' equity 23 147 500; Ordinary share capital 17 875 000; Retained income 5 272 500; Non-current liabilities: Mortgage loan Delta Bank 2 950 000; Current liabilities 4 460 000; Trade and other payables 960 500; Current portion of loan 250 000; Shareholders for dividends 2 475 000; Bank overdraft 774 500. (Fixed assets at carrying value, Cash and cash equivalents and Total assets are shaded and not completed.)

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q6.3

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Maths P1, November 2024, question Q6.3.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2024. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (4 marks)

The graphs of f(x) = -x^2 + 4x + 5 and the straight line g(x) = 2x + 2 are drawn. C(3 ; 8) is a point of intersection of f and g. EH is drawn parallel to the y-axis, with E a point on f and H a point on g (concave-down parabola f with x-intercepts A on the negative x-axis and D on the positive x-axis, turning point B, y-intercept 5; increasing line g through A and C(3 ; 8); vertical segment EH between the two graphs, to the left of C). Calculate the maximum length of EH for f > g.

## Method

maximise vertical distance

## Memo working

The length of the vertical segment EH is the height of f minus the height of g at the same x-value: EH = f(x) - g(x) = -x^2 + 4x + 5 - (2x + 2) = -x^2 + 2x + 3. This is a concave-down parabola in x, so its maximum sits where the derivative is zero: -2x + 2 = 0 -> x = 1. Substitute back: EH = -(1)^2 + 2(1) + 3 = 4. (Memo marking note: the answer alone, without working, earns 1/4.)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

Maximum length of EH = 4

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q6.4

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Maths P1, November 2024, question Q6.4.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2024. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (5 marks)

The graphs of f(x) = -x^2 + 4x + 5 and the straight line g(x) = 2x + 2 are drawn. C(3 ; 8) is a point of intersection of f and g. EH is drawn parallel to the y-axis, with E a point on f and H a point on g (concave-down parabola f with x-intercepts A on the negative x-axis and D on the positive x-axis, turning point B, y-intercept 5; increasing line g through A and C(3 ; 8); vertical segment EH between the two graphs, to the left of C). Given: k(x) = f(x + m) = -x^2 - 2mx - m^2 + 4x + 4m + 5. Determine the value of m such that g is a tangent to k.

## Method

tangency condition derivative

## Memo working

For g to be a tangent to k, the gradient of k at the contact point must equal the gradient of g, which is 2. Differentiate: k'(x) = -2x - 2m + 4. Set k'(x) = 2: -2x - 2m + 4 = 2 -> x = 1 - m. At the contact point the graphs also share the same y-value, so set k(1 - m) = g(1 - m): -(1 - m)^2 - 2m(1 - m) - m^2 + 4(1 - m) + 4m + 5 = 2(1 - m) + 2. Expanding and simplifying leaves -2m - 4 = 0, so m = -2. (Memo option 2: equate k and g and require a double root — the discriminant of x^2 + (2m - 2)x + m^2 - 4m - 3 = 0 must be zero, giving 8m + 16 = 0 -> m = -2. Memo option 3: f'(x) = 2 at x = 1, contact point (1 ; 8), so a horizontal translation of 2 units to the right is needed -> m = -2. Memo marking note: the answer alone earns 0/5.)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

m = -2

## Method

restrict domain for inverse

## Memo working

The parabola fails the horizontal line test: each negative y-value comes from two x-values, one on each side of the turning point. Keeping only one half of the parabola — either the right half or the left half — makes the inverse a function. Either restriction is accepted.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

x >= 0  OR  x <= 0

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q8.3.3

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Maths P1, November 2024, question Q8.3.3.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2024. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (3 marks)

Given: f(x) = -6x^2. Determine the equation of f^(-1) for f^(-1)(x) <= 0. Write your answer in the form y = ...

## Method

inverse of parabola

## Memo working

Start from y = -6x^2 and swap x and y to build the inverse: x = -6y^2. Solve for y: y^2 = -x/6, so y = ±sqrt(-x/6). Since the question requires f^(-1)(x) <= 0, take the negative branch: y = -sqrt(-x/6). The inverse is only defined where -x/6 >= 0, that is for x <= 0.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

y = -sqrt(-x/6), x <= 0

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q3.1.1

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Physical Sciences P1, November 2024, question Q3.1.1.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2024. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (5 marks)

Ball A is thrown vertically upwards at 12 m·s⁻¹ from the top of a building. Two seconds after ball A was thrown upwards, ball B is thrown vertically downwards at 5,4 m·s⁻¹ from the top of the same building. Both balls, A and B, strike the ground at time t seconds. Ignore the effects of air friction. [Graph: position-time sketch graphs for both balls; ball A rises from the top of the building (position Z above the ground) to a maximum position Y, then falls to the ground at time t; ball B starts at Z at 2 s and moves down to the ground, also reaching it at time t.] Using EQUATIONS OF MOTION ONLY, calculate the value of t as shown in the graphs.

## Method

equations of motion simultaneous

## Memo working

Both balls start at the same height and land at the same moment, so write each ball's displacement with Δy = viΔt + ½aΔt² and set them equal. Take upwards as positive, so a = –9,8 m·s⁻². Ball A is in the air for the full t seconds with vi = +12: Δy = 12t + ½(–9,8)t² — equation one. Ball B is thrown 2 s later, so it is in the air for (t – 2) seconds with vi = –5,4: Δy = –5,4(t – 2) + ½(–9,8)(t – 2)² — equation two. Both displacements equal the same drop from the roof to the ground, so set them equal: 12t – 4,9t² = –5,4(t – 2) – 4,9(t – 2)². Expanding the right-hand side, the t² terms cancel, leaving 12t = 14,2t – 8,8, so 2,2t = 8,8 and t = 4 s. (Memo also gives the downwards-as-positive equivalent and options substituting x = t – 2 for ball B or splitting ball A's motion at its turning point, t = 2,45 s.)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

t = 4 s

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q3.1.2

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Physical Sciences P1, November 2024, question Q3.1.2.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2024. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (3 marks)

(Context: ball A is thrown vertically upwards at 12 m·s⁻¹ from the top of a building; 2 s later ball B is thrown vertically downwards at 5,4 m·s⁻¹ from the same rooftop; both strike the ground at t = 4 s.) Using EQUATIONS OF MOTION ONLY, calculate the value of Z, as shown in the graphs. [Z is the starting position of the balls, i.e. the height of the top of the building above the ground.]

## Method

equations of motion displacement

## Memo working

POSITIVE MARKING FROM QUESTION 3.1.1 — use the t = 4 s found there. With upwards positive, substitute either ball's full flight into Δy = viΔt + ½aΔt². Option 1, ball A over the full 4 s: Δy = (12)(4) + ½(–9,8)(4)² = 48 – 78,4 = –30,4 m. The displacement is 30,4 m downwards, so the roof is 30,4 m above the ground: Z = 30,4 m. Option 2, ball B over its (4 – 2) = 2 s of flight: Δy = (–5,4)(2) + ½(–9,8)(2)² = –10,8 – 19,6 = –30,4 m, giving the same Z = 30,4 m. (Memo also gives options using vf² = vi² + 2aΔy with vf = –27,2 m·s⁻¹ or –25 m·s⁻¹, and Δy = ((vi + vf)/2)Δt.)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

Z = 30,4 m

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q3.2

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Physical Sciences P1, November 2024, question Q3.2.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2024. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (4 marks)

(Context: ball A is thrown vertically upwards at 12 m·s⁻¹ from a rooftop at t = 0; ball B is thrown vertically downwards at 5,4 m·s⁻¹ from the same rooftop at t = 2 s; both strike the ground at t = 4 s.) On the same set of axes, sketch the velocity-time graphs for ball A and ball B while they are in free fall. Label the graphs A and B for ball A and ball B respectively. Clearly indicate the following on the graphs: the initial velocity of each ball; the time at which each ball is thrown; the time at which the balls strike the ground.

**Note: the transcribed memo sketch description says line A crosses zero "at 2 s", but from the given data ball A's velocity reaches zero at t = 12/9,8 = 1,22 s. The memo's own marking criteria are consistent with this (they require only that B starts after the time-axis intercept of A); the 2 s in the sketch description appears to reflect the not-to-scale memo drawing. Sketch A's zero crossing at about 1,22 s.**

## Method

velocity time graph sketch

## Memo working

(see marking guidelines) Both balls are in free fall, so both velocity-time graphs are straight lines with the same slope, –9,8 m·s⁻² (taking upwards as positive) — the lines must be parallel. Line A starts at +12 m·s⁻¹ at t = 0, slopes down through zero (at t = 12/9,8, about 1,22 s, where ball A is momentarily at its highest point) and continues into negative values until t = 4 s. Line B starts later, at t = 2 s, at –5,4 m·s⁻¹, and runs parallel to A, lying to the right of A, also ending at t = 4 s. Mark the initial velocities +12 and –5,4, the starting times 0 and 2 s, and the common landing time 4 s. The downwards-positive mirror image of all of this is also accepted.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

[Sketch (upwards positive): straight line A starting at +12 m·s⁻¹ at t = 0 with constant negative slope, crossing zero at 2 s (turning point implied) and ending at 4 s; straight line B starting at –5,4 m·s⁻¹ at t = 2 s, parallel to A and to the right of A, ending at 4 s. Downwards-positive mirror image also accepted.] Marking criteria: correct initial velocities with correct shape (straight lines, both positive or both negative slopes); correct starting times with B starting after the time-axis intercept of A; both graphs end at 4 s (accept t); graphs parallel with B to the right of A. NB: no labels A and B, deduct 1 mark.

## Question (2 marks)

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q2.1

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Physical Sciences P1, November 2024, question Q2.1.

## Question (2 marks)

In an experiment, a crate of mass 8,5 kg, lying stationary on a rough horizontal table, is connected to a mass hanger by means of a light inextensible string passing over a frictionless pulley. Mass pieces are added to the mass hanger and the acceleration of the crate is measured. The experiment is repeated several times by adding different masses to increase the hanging mass each time. Ignore the effects of air friction. [Diagram: 8,5 kg crate on a horizontal table, string over a pulley at the table edge down to a mass hanger with mass pieces.] The results obtained were used to draw a sketch graph of acceleration of crate (m·s⁻²) versus hanging mass (kg): [Graph: acceleration remains zero up to a hanging mass of 4,2 kg, then increases; the acceleration at hanging mass 7,4 kg is labelled Y.] 2.1 Define the term static friction.

## Method

define static friction

## Memo working

(see marking guidelines) This is a definition recall. The key ideas that must appear are: it is a force; it opposes the tendency of motion (not motion itself — the object is still stationary); and it acts relative or parallel to a surface. (Memo instruction: if any of the underlined key words/phrases in the correct context is omitted, deduct 1 mark.)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

The force that opposes the tendency of motion of a stationary object relative/parallel to a surface.

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q2.3.1

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Physical Sciences P1, November 2024, question Q2.3.1.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2024. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (4 marks)

(Context: a crate of mass 8,5 kg on a rough horizontal table is connected by a light inextensible string over a frictionless pulley to a hanging mass; the hanging mass is increased until the crate starts to move.) Calculate the coefficient of static friction (µs). [From the graph the crate starts to move when the hanging mass is 4,2 kg.]

## Method

static friction coefficient

## Memo working

The crate is on the point of moving, so both the crate and the hanging mass are still in equilibrium and static friction is at its maximum value. Step one, the hanging mass: with zero acceleration, Fnet = ma gives mg – T = 0, so the tension equals the hanging weight, T = mg = 4,2(9,8) = 41,16 N. Step two, the crate: horizontally, maximum static friction balances the tension, fs(max) = T. Using fs(max) = µsN with the normal force N equal to the crate's weight on a horizontal table: µs(8,5)(9,8) = 41,16, so µs = 0,49. (Memo option 2: equate fs(max) directly to the hanging weight, µs(8,5)(9,8) = 4,2(9,8), which cancels g to µs(8,5) = 4,2, giving µs = 0,49. Note µs has no unit.)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

µs = 0,49

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q2.4

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Physical Sciences P1, November 2024, question Q2.4.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2024. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (2 marks)

(Context: a crate of mass 8,5 kg on a rough horizontal table is connected by a string over a pulley to a hanging mass.) A 5 kg block is now placed inside the crate and the experiment is repeated. How will this affect the maximum static frictional force now experienced by the crate? Choose from INCREASES, DECREASES or REMAINS THE SAME. Give a reason for the answer.

## Method

friction normal force reasoning

## Memo working

(see marking guidelines) Maximum static friction is fs(max) = µsN. Adding the 5 kg block increases the mass and therefore the weight of the loaded crate, so the table must push up with a larger normal force N. Since fs(max) is directly proportional to N and µs is unchanged (same two surfaces), the maximum static frictional force increases.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

INCREASES. fs(max) ∝ N OR fs(max) ∝ m OR fs(max) = µsN OR the normal force acting on the crate increases OR increase in mass/weight of crate (increases the normal force).

static friction coefficient

NOTE: if the N calculation is not shown, 3/5.)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

µs = 0,38

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q1.3

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Physical Sciences P2, November 2025, question Q1.3.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2025. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (2 marks)

Multiple choice: Which of the following statements ALWAYS apply to compounds that are structural isomers of one another? (i) They belong to the same homologous series. (ii) They have the same structural formula. (iii) They have the same molecular formula. A (iii) only B (i) and (iii) only C (i) and (ii) only D (i), (ii) and (iii)

## Method

multiple choice

## Memo working

(see marking guidelines) Structural isomers are, by definition, compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae. So statement (iii) is always true, and statement (ii) is never true — if the structural formulae were the same, they would be the same compound, not isomers. Statement (i) is not always true either: functional isomers (for example an aldehyde and a ketone with the same molecular formula) are structural isomers that belong to different homologous series. Only (iii) always applies.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

A

## Question (1 mark)

The letters A to G in the table below represent organic compounds: A [structural formula: a four-carbon chain CH3-C(=O)-CH(CH3)-CH3, i.e. carbon 1 is CH3, carbon 2 carries a double-bonded O, carbon 3 carries an H and a methyl branch drawn downward, carbon 4 is CH3]; B [structural formula: a seven-carbon (longest chain) molecule drawn as a six-carbon horizontal chain whose fifth carbon carries a two-carbon branch drawn upward; carbon by carbon along the longest chain: C1 = CH3, C2 carries a Cℓ (drawn below) and a methyl group (drawn above), C3 = CH2, C4 = CH2, C5 carries an H and a methyl group (the sixth carbon of the horizontal row), C6 = the upward branch carbon carrying a Cℓ (drawn left) and an H, C7 = CH3, i.e. 2,6-dichloro-2,5-dimethylheptane]; C CH3CH(CH3)CH2CHO; D C4H10O; E C3H8; F Pentane; G [structural formula drawn as a horizontal row CH3-CH2-C=C-CH3 in which the left doubly-bonded carbon also carries a propyl chain (CH2-CH2-CH3) drawn downward and the right doubly-bonded carbon also carries a methyl group drawn upward, i.e. CH3CH2-C(C3H7)=C(CH3)-CH3, 3-ethyl-2-methylhex-2-ene]. 2.1 Write down the LETTER(S) that represent(s) EACH of the following: 2.1.1 An alcohol

## Method

identify functional group

## Memo working

(see marking guidelines) An alcohol carries the hydroxyl group, –OH, and a saturated alcohol fits the general formula CnH2n+2O. Compound D, C4H10O, matches with n = 4 — butanol. Check the others: A is a ketone (double-bonded O inside the chain), B is a haloalkane (chlorine atoms), C ends in –CHO so it is an aldehyde, E (C3H8) and F (pentane) are alkanes, and G contains a C=C double bond, so it is an alkene. Only D can be the alcohol.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

D

## Question (3 marks)

Write down the IUPAC name of compound A. [Structural formula: CH3-C(=O)-CH(CH3)-CH3.]

## Method

iupac naming

## Memo working

Marking criteria: correct stem, i.e. butanone; substituents (methyl) correctly identified; IUPAC name completely correct including numbering, sequence, hyphens and commas. Working: the longest chain through the carbonyl carbon is four carbons with the C=O inside the chain, so the compound is a ketone with stem butanone. Number from the end nearest the carbonyl so that the carbonyl carbon gets the lowest locant — position 2. The methyl branch then sits on carbon 3, giving 3-methylbutan-2-one.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

3-methylbutan-2-one / 3-methylbutanone (ACCEPT: 3-methyl-2-butanone / methylbutanone)

## Question (3 marks)

Write down the IUPAC name of compound B. [Structural formula: CH3-C(Cℓ)(CH3)-CH2-CH2-CH(CH3)-CH(Cℓ)-CH3 as drawn in the table.]

## Method

iupac naming

## Memo working

Marking criteria: correct stem, i.e. heptane; substituents (dichloro and dimethyl) correctly identified; IUPAC name completely correct including numbering, sequence, hyphens and commas. Working: the longest chain is seven carbons, so the stem is heptane. There are two chlorine atoms and two methyl groups on the chain. Numbering from the end nearest the carbon that carries both a chlorine and a methyl group gives chlorines on carbons 2 and 6 and methyls on carbons 2 and 5 — locant set {2,2,5,6}. Numbering from the other end would give methyls on 3 and 6 — locant set {2,3,6,6}, which is higher at the first point of difference. So the correct name is 2,6-dichloro-2,5-dimethylheptane, with substituents cited alphabetically (chloro before methyl).

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

2,6-dichloro-2,5-dimethylheptane

Write down the IUPAC name of compound G. [Structural formula: CH3CH2CH2-C(CH2CH3)=C(CH3)-CH3 as drawn in the table.]

## Method

iupac naming

## Memo working

Marking criteria: correct stem, i.e. hexene; substituents (ethyl and methyl) correctly identified; IUPAC name completely correct including numbering, sequence, hyphens and commas. Working: choose the longest chain that runs THROUGH the double bond — taking the propyl side into the chain gives six carbons, so the stem is hexene. Number from the end that gives the double bond the lowest locant: starting at the methyl end, the double bond sits between carbons 2 and 3, so hex-2-ene. The methyl branch is on carbon 2 and the ethyl branch on carbon 3. Citing substituents alphabetically (ethyl before methyl) gives 3-ethyl-2-methylhex-2-ene.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

3-ethyl-2-methylhex-2-ene / 3-ethyl-2-methyl-2-hexene

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Physical Sciences P2, November 2025, question Q2.2.4.

## Question (4 marks)

Write down the STRUCTURAL FORMULAE of two STRAIGHT CHAIN positional isomers of compound D (C4H10O).

## Method

structural formulae positional isomers

## Memo working

(see marking guidelines) Compound D, C4H10O, is a four-carbon alcohol. Positional isomers keep the same molecular formula and the same functional group but move that group to a different position on the chain. On a STRAIGHT four-carbon chain the hydroxyl group can sit on carbon 1 or on carbon 2, giving butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol. Draw each as a full structural formula: every carbon shown with all four bonds, every hydrogen shown, and the O-H drawn out. Memo marking criteria per molecule: hydroxyl group on the correct C-atom; whole structure correct. If more than one functional group or a wrong functional group is drawn: 0/2 for that molecule. Condensed structural formulae: maximum 2/4. Bond between O and H not shown: accept.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

Butan-1-ol: full structural formula of a four-carbon straight chain with the hydroxyl (OH) group on the first carbon, all other bonds to H. Butan-2-ol: full structural formula of a four-carbon straight chain with the hydroxyl (OH) group on the second carbon, all other bonds to H.

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q3.1

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Physical Sciences P2, November 2025, question Q3.1.

## Question (1 mark)

Two bottles contain compounds A and B with the same molecular formula, C4H8O2. These compounds are straight chain organic molecules that belong to two different homologous series. [Diagram: two bottles labelled A (C4H8O2) and B (C4H8O2).] The boiling points are used to distinguish between the two compounds. 3.1 Define the term homologous series.

## Method

define homologous series

## Memo working

(see marking guidelines) This is a bookwork definition — learn it word for word. A homologous series is a family of organic compounds sharing one general formula, with each member differing from the next by a single CH2 unit. Either accepted formulation below earns the mark, but a vague answer (for example "compounds with similar properties") earns nothing: the memo marks it 1 or 0.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

A series of organic compounds that can be described by the same general formula. OR: A series of organic compounds in which one member differs from the next by a CH2 group. (1 or 0)

## Question (2 marks)

Identify the TWO homologous series to which these compounds belong. (Refers to QUESTION 3: compounds A and B share the molecular formula C4H8O2, are straight chain molecules, and belong to two different homologous series.)

## Method

identify homologous series

## Memo working

(see marking guidelines) The molecular formula C4H8O2 fits the general formula CnH2nO2 — two oxygens and one degree of unsaturation from a C=O group. The two homologous series in the grade-12 syllabus that match this general formula are the carboxylic acids (for example butanoic acid, CH3CH2CH2COOH) and the esters (for example methyl propanoate or ethyl ethanoate). Since A and B belong to two DIFFERENT series with the same molecular formula, they must be the ester and the carboxylic acid — functional isomers of one another.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

Ester and carboxylic acid

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q12.1

## Question (2 marks)

A company generates a 4-character code using the 26 letters of the alphabet and the 10 digits, from 0 to 9. The code is in the form: letter digit letter digit. Determine how many different codes can be formed if letters and digits may be repeated.

## Method

fundamental counting principle

## Memo working

Multiply the number of choices for each position: 26 choices for the first letter, 10 for the first digit, 26 for the second letter and 10 for the second digit. 26 × 10 × 26 × 10 = 67 600.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

67 600

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q12.2

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Maths P1, November 2024, question Q12.2.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2024. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (4 marks)

A company generates a 4-character code using the 26 letters of the alphabet and the 10 digits, from 0 to 9. The code is in the form: letter digit letter digit. Determine how many different codes can be formed if: the letters D, F, I, Q, U and V may NOT be used; the code may NOT start with a W or a Z; letters or digits may NOT be repeated; the code ends with an odd digit.

## Method

fundamental counting principle with restrictions

## Memo working

With D, F, I, Q, U and V banned, 20 letters remain. First position (letter): also excluding W and Z leaves 18 choices. Last position (digit): must be odd — 5 choices. Second position (digit): any digit except the odd one already used — 9 choices. Third position (letter): any of the 20 allowed letters except the first letter — 19 choices. By the counting principle: 18 × 9 × 19 × 5 = 15 390.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

15 390

percentage increase

## Question (2 marks)

Eight runners compete in a race where there are no tied finishes. Bongi and Andrew are two of the competitors. Calculate the total number of possible ways in which the 8 runners can finish the race if Bongi finishes in a position immediately after Andrew.

## Method

treat pair as unit

## Memo working

Since Bongi must finish immediately after Andrew, treat the pair Andrew-Bongi as a single unit in that fixed order. That leaves 7 objects to arrange (the pair plus the other 6 runners): 7! = 7 · 6! = 5 040 ways.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q11.3.2

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Maths P1, November 2025, question Q11.3.2.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2025. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (4 marks)

Eight runners compete in a race where there are no tied finishes. Bongi and Andrew are two of the competitors. Calculate the probability that TWO OR MORE runners finish the race after Andrew and before Bongi.

## Method

count gap arrangements probability

## Memo working

Count the favourable finishes where Andrew and Bongi are separated by 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 of the other runners, with Andrew ahead. If exactly k runners separate them, the pair occupies positions i and i + k + 1, which can be placed in 7 - k ways, and the other 6 runners fill the remaining positions in 6! ways. Summing for k = 2 to 6: 5×6! + 4×6! + 3×6! + 2×6! + 1×6! = 6!(15) favourable outcomes. The total number of finishes is 8!, so P = 6!(15)/8! = 15/56 = 0,27. (Alternative memo method uses the complement: [8! - (7!·2 + 2·6·6!)]/(8!·2) = 21 600/80 640 = 15/56.)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

15/56 = 0,27

Consider the reaction below: 2Ag(s) + Pb²⁺(aq) → 2Ag⁺(s) + Pb(s). By means of a calculation, determine whether this reaction is SPONTANEOUS or NON-SPONTANEOUS.

**Note: the paper prints the product as '2Ag⁺(s)'; the phase should read (aq). Transcribed verbatim — flagged as a source typo.**

## Method

cell potential spontaneity

## Memo working

OPTION 1: E°cell = E°reduction − E°oxidation = –0,13 – (0,80) = –0,93 V; the negative cell potential means the reaction is non-spontaneous. OPTION 2: Pb²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Pb, E° = –0,13 V; 2Ag → 2Ag⁺ + 2e⁻, E° = –0,80 V; overall Pb²⁺ + 2Ag → Pb + 2Ag⁺, E° = –0,93 V; non-spontaneous. (Accept any other correct formula from the data sheet; unconventional abbreviations, e.g. E°cell = E°OA − E°RA, with correct substitutions: 3/4 of the formula-related marks.)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

E°cell = –0,93 V, therefore non-spontaneous

## Question (2 marks)

Multiple choice: A galvanic cell consists of the following half-cells: Fe3+(aq)|Fe2+(aq) and Ni2+(aq)|Ni(s). Which ONE of the following statements is CORRECT for this cell? A Ni2+ is reduced and Fe2+ is oxidised. B Ni2+ is oxidised and Fe3+ is reduced. C Pt is the electrode at the cathode. D Ni is the electrode at the cathode.

## Method

multiple choice

## Memo working

(see marking guidelines) Compare the standard electrode potentials from the table: E°(Fe3+/Fe2+) = +0,77 V is higher than E°(Ni2+/Ni) = −0,27 V, so Fe3+ is the stronger oxidising agent. In the spontaneous cell, Fe3+ is reduced to Fe2+ at the CATHODE, and Ni is oxidised to Ni2+ at the ANODE. That eliminates A (reversed direction), B (Ni2+ cannot be oxidised at the anode; it is Ni metal that is oxidised) and D (the nickel electrode is the anode, not the cathode). The Fe3+|Fe2+ half-cell contains only ions in solution — no solid conductor — so it needs an inert platinum electrode, and that platinum electrode is the cathode.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

C

standard conditions mass calculation

Step 4 — convert to mass with M(Aℓ2(SO4)3) = 342 g·mol⁻¹: m = nM = 0,125 x 342 = 42,75 g.

Marking criteria: (a) calculate n(Aℓ3+); (b) use mole ratio n(Aℓ2(SO4)3) : n(Aℓ3+) = 1 : 2; (c) multiply n(Aℓ2(SO4)3) by M = 342; (d) final correct answer 42,75 g.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

m(Aℓ2(SO4)3) = 42,75 g

## Question (5 marks)

An AC generator operates a fan. The resistance of the fan is 60 Ω and the maximum potential difference produced by the generator is 311,11 V. Calculate the cost of operating the fan for 1,5 hours if the cost of electricity is R3,33 per kWh.

## Method

rms power cost calculation

## Memo working

First convert the maximum potential difference to the rms value: Vrms = Vmax/√2 = 311,11/√2 = 219,99 V.

Next find the average power dissipated in the fan: Pave = Vrms²/R = (219,99)²/60 = 806,59 W, which is 0,80659 kW.

Finally, cost = power x time x tariff = 0,80659(1,5)(3,33) = R4,03. (Equivalently, energy E = PΔt = 0,80659 x 1,5 = 1,21 kWh, and cost = E x tariff = 1,21(3,33) = R4,03.)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

Cost = R4,03

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q3.1

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Maths P1, November 2024, question Q3.1.

## Question (2 marks)

A circle with radius 6 cm is drawn. A second, smaller circle is drawn through the centre of the first circle and also touches the first circle internally, as shown in the diagram. A third, smaller circle is drawn through the centre of the second circle and touches the second circle internally. The process of drawing circles continues and forms a geometric pattern. (Figure: three nested circles, each smaller circle passing through the centre of the previous circle and touching it internally at the top.) Write down the radius of the 3rd circle.

## Method

geometric sequence term

## Memo working

Each new circle passes through the centre of the previous one and touches it internally, so its diameter equals the previous radius — each radius is half the one before. 2nd circle: 6/2 = 3 cm; 3rd circle: 3/2 = 1,5 cm (or directly 6(1/2)^2 = 1,5).

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q3.3

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Maths P1, November 2024, question Q3.3.

## Question (4 marks)

Which circle (in the pattern with radii 6 ; 3 ; 1,5 ; ... cm, each half the previous) has a diameter of 3/128 cm?

## Method

geometric sequence solve n

## Memo working

A diameter of 3/128 means a radius of (1/2)(3/128) = 3/256. Set the general term equal to it: 6(1/2)^(n-1) = 3/256, so (1/2)^(n-1) = 1/512 = (1/2)^9. Equate exponents: n - 1 = 9 -> n = 10. (Memo alternative: work with diameters 12 ; 6 ; 3 ; ... and solve 3/128 = 12(1/2)^(n-1).)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

n = 10 (the 10th circle)

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q2.1.1

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Maths P1, November 2025, question Q2.1.1.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2025. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (3 marks)

Given the infinite geometric series: (t + 10) + (t - 2) + (t + 4) + ... Show that t = -2

## Method

equate common ratios

## Memo working

In a geometric series the ratio between consecutive terms is constant, so (t - 2)/(t + 10) = (t + 4)/(t - 2). Cross multiply: (t - 2)^2 = (t + 4)(t + 10). Expand both sides: t^2 - 4t + 4 = t^2 + 14t + 40. The t^2 terms cancel, leaving -18t = 36, so t = -2. (With t = -2 the series is 8 - 4 + 2 - ..., a genuine geometric series with r = -1/2.)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

t = -2

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q2.1.2

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Maths P1, November 2025, question Q2.1.2.

## Question (3 marks)

Calculate the value of T25. Write your answer in the form Tn = b^x  (For the geometric series of Q2.1.1 with t = -2, i.e. 8 - 4 + 2 - ...)

## Method

geometric term exponential form

## Memo working

With t = -2 the series is 8 ; -4 ; 2 ; ... so a = 8 and r = -4/8 = -1/2. The general term is Tn = a·r^(n-1), so T25 = 8(-1/2)^24. Since 24 is even, (-1/2)^24 = (1/2)^24, and 8 = 2^3, so T25 = 2^3 · 2^(-24) = 2^(-21) = (1/2)^21.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

T25 = (1/2)^21  OR  T25 = 2^(-21)  OR  T25 = 8^(-7)  OR  T25 = 128^(-3)  OR  T25 = (2 097 152)^(-1)

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q3.1.3

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Geography P1, November 2025, question Q3.1.3.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2025. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (4 marks)

Calculate the average gradient from 6 in block E5 to 7 in block D5 on the orthophoto map. Use the following information: Vertical interval (VI) = 60 m. Formula: Vertical Interval (VI) / Horizontal Equivalent (HE) (4 x 1)

(Based on the 1 : 10 000 orthophoto map 3318 DD 18 STELLENBOSCH. The map sheet is a separate physical sheet; the distance between points 6 and 7 measured off the map for the memo is 3,8 cm, with 3,7 cm - 3,9 cm accepted.)

## Method

gradient calculation

## Memo working

The vertical interval is given: VI = 60 m. The horizontal equivalent is the real ground distance between the two points. Measure the map distance — 3,8 cm (1) — and convert it using the orthophoto scale of 1 : 10 000, where 1 cm on the map is 100 m on the ground: HE = 3,8 x 100 = 380 (1) m [measurement range 3,7 cm - 3,9 cm, so 370 m - 390 m]. Substitute into the formula: Gradient = VI/HE = 60/380 (1) (mark for correct substitution). Divide both sides by 60 to express it as one metre of climb per so many metres of distance: 1 : 6,33 (1) [accepted range 1 : 6,16 - 1 : 6,50].

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

1 : 6,33 (1) [accepted range 1:6,16 - 1:6,50]

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q7.1

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Maths P1, November 2024, question Q7.1.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2024. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (3 marks)

Mary's grandparents deposited R5 000 into a savings account on the day that she was born. The account pays interest at a rate of 6,8% p.a., compounded quarterly. Calculate the accumulated amount in this account on Mary's 16th birthday.

## Method

compound interest

## Memo working

Use the compound growth formula A = P(1 + i)^n. The quarterly interest rate is the annual rate divided by four: i = 6,8/400. Over 16 years there are 16 × 4 = 64 quarterly compounding periods. A = 5 000(1 + 6,8/400)^64 = R14 706,56.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

R14 706,56

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q7.2

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Maths P1, November 2024, question Q7.2.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2024. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (2 marks)

After 4 years, the value of a printer was half of its original value. Determine the rate at which the value of the printer depreciated over this period, if depreciation was calculated according to a straight-line method.

## Method

straight line depreciation

## Memo working

Straight-line depreciation uses A = P(1 - in). Half the original value after 4 years means (1/2)P = P(1 - 4i). Divide by P and solve: 4i = 1/2 -> i = 1/8, so r = 12,5%. (Or directly: the printer loses 50% of its value in 4 years, so r = 50%/4 = 12,5% per year.)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

r = 12,5%

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q6

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Economics P1, November 2024, question Q6.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2024. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (40 marks)

QUESTION 6: ECONOMIC PURSUITS

- Discuss in detail the demand-side approach in promoting economic growth and development in South Africa. (26 marks)
- Analyse the importance of promoting small businesses for the South African economy. (10 marks)

(Section C essay: candidates answer ONE of the two 40-mark essay questions. The same essay rubric as Question 5 applies: introduction maximum 2 marks; body main part maximum 26 marks, with a maximum of 8 marks for headings/examples; body additional part maximum 10 marks, with a maximum of 2 marks for mere listing of facts; conclusion maximum 2 marks.)

## Method

essay

## Memo working

(see marking guidelines)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

INTRODUCTION (maximum 2 marks)

The demand-side approach involves discretionary changes in monetary and fiscal policies with the aim of changing the level of aggregate demand and therefore output. (Accept any other correct relevant introduction)

BODY MAIN PART (maximum 26 marks) — THE SOUTH AFRICAN DEMAND-SIDE APPROACH

The South African government uses both monetary and fiscal policies for stabilisation purposes. It uses monetary policies, through the SARB, mainly to stabilise prices during the long upswings of the business cycles. The government uses fiscal policy to meet social development and economic growth.

Monetary policy: The SARB, as the central bank, is responsible for formulating South Africa's monetary policy and is largely responsible for implementing this policy. Its primary goal, as defined in the Constitution, is to protect the value of the currency, by stabilising prices in terms of inflation targets. It uses mainly the following monetary policy instruments:

1. Interest rate changes: In South Africa interest rates are used to influence credit creation by making credit more expensive or cheaper. To stimulate economic growth, the SARB may reduce interest rates to make borrowing cheaper which will encourage consumer spending and encourage production. Interest rates are used to stabilise the exchange rate by encouraging capital inflows or outflows in order to take care of a deficit or a surplus on the current account of the balance of payments.
2. Open market transactions: To restrict bank credit, the SARB may sell securities on open markets which results in money flowing from the banks to the SARB and cannot extend credit. To encourage credit creation, the SARB buys securities on open markets leading to money flowing into the banking system and used to extend credit.
3. Moral suasion: The SARB consults with banks and persuades them to act in a manner that is desirable in terms of the economic conditions that prevail at the time. The persuasion is often linked to transactions of the SARB in the money market, for example buying and selling paper such as bills and bonds. For instance, if banks are too generous in extending credit, the SARB can call on them to be stricter. To encourage credit extension, the SARB may persuade commercial banks to be more lenient when granting credit to their clients.
4. Cash reserves requirement: To restrict bank credit, the SARB may increase the cash reserve requirement which reduces credit extension by banks. To encourage credit creation, the SARB decreases the cash reserve requirement to allow banks to extend more credit to the public. Access to more credit will increase consumer spending and investments which will stimulate economic growth.

Fiscal policy: South Africa's fiscal policy is put into practice by means of the budgetary process. The main purpose of fiscal policy in South Africa is to stimulate macroeconomic growth and employment, and to ensure a desirable redistribution of income (economic equity). The price stability and exchange rates stability objectives are left for the most part to monetary policy. The government compiles its expenditure and taxation in a way that enhances its chances of achieving its macroeconomic objectives. In South Africa, fiscal policy includes the following elements:

1. Progressive personal income tax: Higher-income earners are taxed at higher rates than lower-income earners. The taxes are used to finance social development. Tax revenue will benefit the poor through social grants and social allowances such as pensions.
2. Wealth taxes: Properties such as houses, offices and factory buildings in urban areas are taxed annually (Property tax). Transfer duties are paid when properties are bought. Securities (shares and bonds) are taxed when they are traded. Capital gains tax (CGT) is levied on gains earned on the sale of capital goods, such as properties and shares. Estate duties are levied on the estates of deceased persons with a value of more than R3,5 million. Taxes are used to finance development expenditures which benefit the poor more than those who are not poor.
3. Cash benefits: The government provides social security payments such as old-age pensions, disability grants, child support grants, foster child grant, unemployment insurance and the social relief of distress (SRD) grant.
4. Benefits in kind/Natural/Natura benefits: Benefits in kind include the provision of healthcare, education and school meals, protection, municipal services and infrastructure. Where user-fees are charged, poor people and low-income earners benefit more than others because they pay nothing or less than higher-income earners. For instance, Free basic electricity (FBE) of 50kWh per household per month and Free basic water (FBW) of 6 kl (6 000 litres) of water per month per household are provided.
5. Other redistribution methods: Some macroeconomic policies have advantages that favour poor and low-income earners. Public works programmes provide employment and strategic integrated projects (SIPs), provide employment subsidies and a number of other cash and financial benefits to SMMEs. Previously disadvantaged persons receive first preference to redress the imbalance of the past.
6. Land restitution and land redistribution: The purpose of land restitution is to return land (or pay cash compensation) to those who lost their land because of discriminatory laws of the past. Land redistribution focuses on land for residential (town) and productive (farm) use. The aim is to redistribute 30% of the country's agricultural land to previously disadvantaged persons. The funds for land restitution and land redistribution programmes are provided for in the main budget.
7. Property subsidies: Subsidies help beneficiaries to acquire ownership of fixed residential property. The government's housing subsidy scheme provides funding options to all eligible persons earning a specified range of monthly income. A housing subsidy is not a cash pay-out but it is paid directly to the financial institution providing the housing bond or to the seller. The subsidy depends on a person's income but the lower the income, the higher the subsidy. The housing subsidy scheme is financed from the main budget.

(Accept any other correct relevant response) (Allocate a maximum of 8 marks for headings/subheadings/examples)

ADDITIONAL PART (maximum 10 marks)

- Small businesses can help to create employment for those who are structurally unemployed in the economy thereby reducing the unemployment rate.
- Small businesses may compete with larger businesses which improves economic efficiency and promotes innovation.
- Output produced by small businesses contributes to the GDP of the country thereby stimulating economic growth.
- Small businesses may create a source of income for the households which helps to alleviate poverty in South Africa.
- The establishment of small businesses may expand the tax base which increases tax revenue for the government.
- Output produced by small businesses may contribute to an increase in exports which helps to reduce balance of payments (BOP) problems.
- Promotion of small businesses may help to encourage skills development amongst the South African population.
- The population percentage that depends on social grants may decrease thereby reduce the welfare expenditure for the government.
- Tax revenue collected from small business may increase the financial capacity of the government to develop infrastructure.

(Accept any other correct relevant response) (A maximum of 2 marks may be allocated for mere listing of facts/examples)

CONCLUSION (maximum 2 marks)

The government should complement demand-side policies with supply-side policies to achieve higher economic growth. (Accept any other relevant higher order conclusion.)

recall

Natural rate of unemployment

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Economics P1, November 2025, question Q3.4.

## Question (8 marks)

Briefly discuss the Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment Programme (BBBEE) and the National Skills Development Strategy (NSDS) as South African growth and development policies and strategic initiatives. (2 x 4)

## Method

discussion

## Memo working

(see marking guidelines)

Teachable steps: two headings, four marks each. BBBEE: a legal framework for transforming the South African economy by promoting inclusive economic participation for black South Africans — redress and affirmative action in the workplace pursued through preferential procurement, enterprise development, skills development and the promotion of ownership and management. NSDS: a strategy to improve the skills of the labour force so as to meet economic needs, reduce unemployment and promote equity — radically transforming education and training, targeting skills in high demand, building partnerships between educational institutions, employers and SETAs, and prioritising historically disadvantaged groups.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

**Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment Programme (BBBEE)**

- BBBEE promotes inclusive economic participation for black South Africans to address historical inequalities.
- The strategy provides a legal basis for the transformation of the South African economy.
- The objectives are redress and affirmative action in the workplace and business environments.
- BBBEE promotes growth and development through preferential procurement, enterprise development, skills development, and the promotion of ownership and management.

(Accept any other correct relevant response)

**National Skills Development Strategy (NSDS)**

- The NSDS aims to improve the skills of the South African labour force to meet economic needs, reduce unemployment, and promote equity.
- The NSDS is intended to radically transform education and training in South Africa.
- The strategy identifies and provides training for skills that are in high demand to boost economic productivity.
- The NSDS improves the quality training programs, through partnerships between educational institutions, employers, and SETAs.
- The strategy focuses on providing skills acquisition opportunities to historically disadvantaged groups, to transform racial and gender inequalities in the labour force.

(Accept any other correct relevant response. Memo note: a maximum of 4 marks may be allocated for mere listing of facts/examples.)

diagram interpretation

Wind A blows in from the high off the south-west coast, across the cold Atlantic — so it arrives cold and dry. Wind B blows in from the high over the warm Indian Ocean — so it arrives warm and moist. Where these two contrasting airmasses meet, the moisture front and its line of thunderstorms develop.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

- WIND A (south-westerly): cold and dry (2)
- WIND B (north-easterly): warm and moist (2)

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q1.5.3

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Geography P1, November 2024, question Q1.5.3.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2024. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (4 marks)

(Refer to a source on line thunderstorms over South Africa: 'During summer, thunderstorms can form a line that can extend for hundreds of kilometres. These line thunderstorms can persist for many hours and produce damaging winds and hail, which impacts negatively on the natural environment.' A sketch map of South Africa shows a north-west to south-east moisture front across the interior with cumulonimbus clouds along it at A and B. Wind A blows in from a high off the south-west coast towards the moisture front; wind B blows in from a high off the east coast over the Indian Ocean. An inset diagram grades rainfall outward from the moisture front: heavy rain nearest the front, then moderate rain, then light rain furthest away.) Explain why the heaviest rainfall occurs closest to the moisture front, as evident in the source. (2 x 2)

## Method

process explanation

Along the moisture front the contrast between the two airmasses forces the most rapid uplift, so condensation is deepest and a dense line of cumulonimbus clouds builds there. Moving away from the front, uplift weakens, condensation lessens and cloud thins — so rainfall grades from heavy at the front to light far from it. Answer from either side of that contrast, but stay explicitly close to or far from the front.

## Memo working

(see marking guidelines)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

- Close to the moisture front: Rapid uplift of air along the moisture front (2); Greater (vertical) condensation (2); (Dense line of) cumulonimbus clouds form (2)
- OR Further from the moisture front: Less uplift of air further from the moisture front (2); Less (vertical) condensation (2); Less clouds form (2)

[ANY TWO - MUST REFER TO EITHER CLOSE TO OR FURTHER FROM MOISTURE FRONT]

An inset diagram grades rainfall outward from the moisture front: heavy rain nearest the front, then moderate rain, then light rain furthest away.) Explain the negative physical (natural) impact of line thunderstorms. (3 x 2)

## Method

impact explanation

Keep the focus on the natural environment, not people or property: habitats and ecosystems destroyed and biodiversity reduced; topsoil washed away and soils leached; mass movements triggered on slopes; wildlife displaced or drowned; trees and natural vegetation uprooted; water quality reduced; sinkholes forming; and channels silting up with deposited material. Any three, explained, at two marks each.

## Memo working

(see marking guidelines)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

- Natural habitats will be destroyed (2)
- Ecosystems will be destroyed (2)
- Biodiversity will be reduced (2)
- Top soil will be washed away/soil erosion (2)
- Mass movements can be triggered (accept examples) (2)
- Wildlife would be displaced/drowned (2)
- Trees/natural vegetation can be uprooted/destroyed (2)
- Water quality will be reduced (2)
- Increased leaching of soil (2)
- Sinkholes form (2)
- Silting up/deposition of material (2)

[ANY THREE]

## Question (1 mark)

(Synoptic weather map interpretation: complete the statement in COLUMN A with the correct option from COLUMN B. Write only Y or Z.) The name of the air pressure cell that dominates the interior of South Africa in winter  [Y heat low / Z Kalahari high]

## Method

column matching

In winter the interior plateau cools down and the subtropical high-pressure belt shifts northwards, so a strong high-pressure cell — the Kalahari High — settles over the interior of South Africa and dominates its winter weather. The heat low is the opposite case: a summer feature that forms when intense surface heating makes air rise over the interior.

## Memo working

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

Z (Kalahari high)

## Method

column matching

Mid-latitude cyclones travel from west to east south of the country. When the South Indian High sits to the south-east, directly in a cyclone's path, it blocks the cyclone's eastward movement and forces it to slow or divert — that is why it is called a blocking high. The Kalahari High sits over the interior plateau, not in the cyclone's path.

## Method

column matching

The sketch shows moist Indian Ocean air and drier air from the south-west converging along a north-west to south-east moisture front over the interior. Where the two air masses meet, the moist air is forced to rise, building a long band of cumulonimbus clouds along the front — that produces line thunderstorms. Berg winds are hot, dry offshore winds descending from the plateau in winter and have nothing to do with a moisture front.

Y (line thunderstorms)

## Method

column matching

Read the station models. On a wind shaft each full feather represents 10 knots, so Cape Town's shaft with two full feathers shows a 20-knot wind, and its fully shaded station circle shows overcast conditions, which fit rainfall. Durban's shaft carries no feathers at all, so there is no 20-knot wind there. Cape Town is therefore the station where rainfall with 20 knots of wind is likely.

Z (Cape Town (CT))

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q1.5.3

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Geography P1, November 2025, question Q1.5.3.

## Question (4 marks)

Explain the processes that lead to berg winds being warm and dry. (2 x 2)  (Synoptic weather map of southern Africa showing berg wind conditions: a high (1016 hPa) over the interior, a low to the north-west and a coastal low off the south/south-east coast with tightly packed isobars near Cape Town; station models give temperature/dew point pairs including East London 34/10, Durban 27/10 and Cape Town 12/12; the caption warns of extremely hot conditions above 30 degrees C across the Eastern Cape.)

## Method

process explanation

## Memo working

Deal with temperature and moisture separately - the memo requires both. Temperature: air from the interior plateau descends down the escarpment towards the coast; as it sinks it is compressed and heated adiabatically at about 1 degree C per 100 m. Moisture: as the descending air warms, its relative humidity drops and moisture is evaporated, so the wind reaches the coast warm and dry.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

TEMPERATURE: The air descends (from the interior) down the escarpment (2); The air is heated adiabatically (1 °C/100 m) (2) [ANY ONE]. MOISTURE: Moisture is evaporated as air descends (from the interior to the coast) (2). [MUST INCLUDE TEMPERATURE AND MOISTURE]

interpret interval rule

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q2.1.3

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Maths P2, November 2025, question Q2.1.3.

## Question (3 marks)

Draw a histogram to represent the information provided in the cumulative frequency table. (Cumulative frequency table from QUESTION 2.1: 0 < t ≤ 20 -> 16; 0 < t ≤ 40 -> 40; 0 < t ≤ 60 -> 59; 0 < t ≤ 80 -> 67; 0 < t ≤ 100 -> 70.)

## Method

histogram from cumulative frequencies

## Memo working

First convert cumulative frequencies to class frequencies by subtracting each cumulative total from the next: 16; 40 - 16 = 24; 59 - 40 = 19; 67 - 59 = 8; 70 - 67 = 3. Then draw one bar per interval — (0;20], (20;40], (40;60], (60;80], (80;100] — with heights 16, 24, 19, 8 and 3, and with no gaps between the bars. Memo awards: two frequencies correct; all frequencies correct; no gaps between bars.

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

Histogram with class frequencies 16 ; 24 ; 19 ; 8 ; 3 for the intervals (0;20], (20;40], (40;60], (60;80], (80;100]

## Method

annualise income and identify tax bracket

## Memo working

The tax table works on ANNUAL taxable income, but Miecke's income is given per month, so first annualise it: Annual taxable income = R39 275,85 x 12 (1MA multiplying by 12) = R471 310,20 (1A simplification). Now place this amount in the table: R471 310,20 falls between R370 501 and R512 800, which is Tax Bracket C (1MCA). AO

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

Tax Bracket C

income tax with rebate

Miecke is 45, so only the primary rebate applies: Annual tax payable = R108 613,162 - R17 235 (1RT rebate: R17 235) = R91 378,16 (1CA simplification). She gets no medical tax credits because she has no medical aid. (CA from Question 2.3.1.)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

R91 378,16

fraction of total contribution

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

R1 265,77

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q2.1.4c

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Mathematical Literacy P1, November 2025, question Q2.1.4c.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2025. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (8 marks)

Muriel Davids (42 years old) earns a gross salary of R35 000 per month; she does not contribute to a pension fund, so her gross salary is her taxable income. She pays medical aid for herself only and receives no bonus. Her monthly PAYE deduction, read from the deduction table in ANNEXURE A, is R6 298. The 2024/2025 annual tax rates in ANNEXURE A give her bracket as R77 362 + 31% of taxable income above R370 500, a primary rebate of R17 235 and a monthly medical tax credit of R364 for the taxpayer. (c) Muriel stated that she overpaid tax in the 2024/2025 tax year. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether her statement is VALID.

## Method

income tax with rebate and medical credit verification

## Memo working

First annualise the income: Annual taxable income = R35 000 × 12 = R420 000 (1A). Apply the tax bracket rule: Annual tax payable before rebates = R77 362 + 31% of (R420 000 - R370 500) (1MCA correct tax bracket) = R77 362 + 31% of R49 500 = R77 362 + R15 345 = R92 707,00 (1CA). Now subtract the primary rebate and a year of medical tax credits: Annual tax payable after rebates = R92 707,00 - R17 235 (1RT correct tax rebate) - (R364 × 12) = R92 707,00 - R17 235 - R4 368 (1MA subtracting MTC) = R71 104,00 (1CA). Convert to a monthly amount: Monthly tax payable = R71 104,00 ÷ 12 = R5 925,33 — but R6 298 was deducted each month. (Equivalently: annual tax actually deducted = R6 298 × 12 = R75 576, against R71 104,00 actually payable; 1CA tax amount, CA from Question 2.1.4(a).) She paid more than she owed, so her statement is VALID (1O conclusion). (The bracket values, rebate and medical tax credit are as printed in the memo; the annexure itself sits in the Special Answer Book. Arithmetic verified: R75 576 deducted vs R71 104 payable.)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

Annual taxable income = R420 000; annual tax payable after rebates = R71 104,00; monthly tax payable = R5 925,33 (or annual PAYE deducted = R6 298 × 12 = R75 576). Her statement is VALID.

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q5.1.3

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Mathematical Literacy P1, November 2025, question Q5.1.3.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2025. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (5 marks)

Candice started a small delivery business in London and chose car purchase OPTION A, whose deposit and first-month instalment is £1 173,66. Candice's aunt in Switzerland offers to pay the deposit and first-month instalment. TABLE 9 shows the currency conversion factors: for the Swiss franc (CHF), 20,48 ZAR per unit and 0,049 units per ZAR; for the pound sterling (£), 23,20 ZAR per unit and 0,043 units per ZAR. Calculate, in Swiss franc (CHF), the deposit and first-month instalment for OPTION A.

## Method

two step currency conversion

## Memo working

Deposit and first-month instalment = £1 173,66 (1RT). Amount in rand = £1 173,66 / 0,043 (1MA exchange rate) = R27 294,42 (1CA). Amount in CHF = R27 294,42 / R20,48 (1MCA exchange rate) = CHF 1 332,74 (1CA) OR R27 294,42 x 0,049 = CHF 1 337,43. OR via £1 173,66 x R23,20 = R27 228,91; /20,48 = CHF 1 329,54 OR x 0,049 = CHF 1 334,22. OR conversion rate £1 = CHF 23,20/20,48 = 1,1328125 (1MA, 1CA); 1 173,66 x 1,1328125 = CHF 1 329,54. (The memo accepts several answers depending on which of the rounded conversion factors are used: 1 329,54 / 1 332,74 / 1 334,22 / 1 337,43.)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

CHF 1 332,74 (alternatives in memo: CHF 1 337,43; CHF 1 329,54; CHF 1 334,22)

## Method

explanation

## Memo working

(see marking guidelines)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

- Production output may decrease which may slow down economic growth and increase unemployment.

- Workers may lose their jobs which leads to a decrease in demand for goods and services in the economy.
- As workers lose their jobs due to low productivity, unemployment may increase in the economy.

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q4.4

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Economics P1, November 2024, question Q4.4.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2024. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (8 marks)

Discuss the social indicators that relate to nutrition. (4 x 2)

## Method

discussion

## Memo working

(see marking guidelines)

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

a) Child malnutrition

- Malnutrition is expressed in two ways - weight for age (under-weight) and height for age (dwarfism).
- The proportion of underweight children is the most important indicator of malnutrition.
- In South Africa, malnutrition is one of the leading causes of child deaths, and the number of affected children is increasing.
- The main causes of childhood malnutrition are household food insecurity, inadequate care and unhealthy household environment, and lack of health care services.

b) Overweight children/Obesity

- An overweight child is one who weighs more when compared on an index to a child of the same age, gender and height.
- Obesity of children is associated with diseases such as diabetes and psychological disorder.
- Disease caused by obesity may impact directly on the productivity of the individual and place an enormous strain no public health sector.
- South Africa has a combined overweight and obesity prevalence in children which is higher than the global average.

(Accept any other correct relevant response. Memo note: a maximum of 4 marks may be allocated for mere listing of facts/examples.)

**Note on a source anomaly:** the official memo phrase "enormous strain no public health sector" is a verbatim misprint for "on public health sector". It is transcribed verbatim above.

# Past-Paper Worked Example — Q3.5

**Source:** Department of Basic Education — Grade 12 Economics P1, November 2025, question Q3.5.

**© Department of Basic Education, 2025. Reproduced for educational use with attribution.**

## Question (8 marks)

How can changes in the various economic indicators be used to show improvement in the performance of the economy? (4 x 2)

## Method

discussion

## Memo working

(see marking guidelines)

Teachable steps: choose any four indicators and, for two marks each, state the direction of change and explain why it signals improvement: a falling CPI (lower cost of living lifts demand); a falling PPI (lower production costs encourage output); improving terms of trade (more export income to finance imports, a healthier current account); a higher employment rate (more spending, tax revenue and growth); higher labour productivity (efficiency and competitiveness); interest-rate movements (lower rates stimulate spending and investment, higher rates curb inflation and attract foreign investment); exchange-rate movements (a weaker rand makes exports more competitive, a stronger rand cheapens imports and reduces inflation); or growing money supply (more liquidity and credit for short-term spending).

## Answer (per marking guidelines)

- A decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) shows lower cost of living in the economy which triggers an increase in demand for goods and services.
- A decline in the Producer Price Index (PPI) indicates lower cost of production and encourages the production of more goods and services.
- An improvement in the terms of trade means that South Africa gets more income for exports which is used to finance import expenditure, strengthening economic stability in the short term.
- An improved terms of trade may reflect a surplus in the current account which serves as a yardstick for a healthy economy.
- A higher employment rate reflects economic stability which boosts consumer spending, tax revenues, and economic growth.
- Higher labour productivity indicates enhanced economic efficiency, competitiveness, and GDP growth.
- Lower interest rates encourage spending and investment to boost economic activity.
- Higher interest rates curb inflation and attracts foreign investment which will lead to an increase in economic growth.
- A weaker exchange rate means results in exports becoming cheaper and more competitive in the global market which improves the trade balance of the current account.
- A stronger exchange rate shows that the country will pay less for imports which reduces inflation.
- An increase in money supply (M1, M2 and M3) reflects higher liquidity, expanding credit availability and boosting short-term spending.

(Accept any other correct relevant response. Memo note: a maximum of 2 marks may be allocated for mere listing of facts/examples.)

**Note on a source anomaly:** the official memo bullet 'A weaker exchange rate means results in exports becoming cheaper and more competitive in the global market which improves the trade balance of the current account' contains a verbatim misprint ('means results'). It is transcribed verbatim above.
